import RouterProvider.description:
Data mode provider for browser apps.
Import it from `react-router/dom` — that build integrates with `flushSync` and view transitions. The one exported from `react-router` targets non-DOM renderers.

RouterProvider.description: Renders a router created by `createBrowserRouter` and friends. Replaces `<BrowserRouter>` in Data mode.

Data mode entry.description: Complete Data mode setup — router definition plus mount. The mode to pick when you want loaders and actions without the Framework build.

import BrowserRouter.description: Declarative mode router using the History API.

BrowserRouter.description:
Declarative mode only — no loaders, actions or pending states.
For data features use `createBrowserRouter` + `<RouterProvider>`.

import HashRouter.description: Declarative router storing the location in the URL hash.

HashRouter.description: Keeps the location after `#`. For static hosts that cannot rewrite every path to index.html.

MemoryRouter.description: No URL involved — the router of choice for tests and React Native.

StaticRouter.description: Renders a fixed location on the server. Declarative mode SSR only — no data loading.

import StaticRouterProvider.description: Server counterpart of `RouterProvider` for Data mode SSR.

StaticRouterProvider.description:
Renders a static router built by `createStaticRouter`, using the context from `createStaticHandler().query()`.
The Data mode SSR pair — Framework mode handles this itself.

ServerRouter.description: Renders the matched routes on the server. Used inside `entry.server.tsx`.

Router.description: The primitive the other routers build on. Only reach for it when implementing a custom history integration.
